A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NMR experimental data and the theoretically calculated (B3LYP) chemical shifts are in good agreement and that the 15N NHR and 15N HMR chemical shifts are the best probe for the "tautomers" in solution.

the 1H and 13C chemical shifts are the most sensitive to tautomerism, whereas 15N is less sensitive and the 2D-1H/1H-NOESY experiments are the most useful for assigning the tautomeric positions in solution.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 15N NHR chemical shifts are a good probe of the "tautomers" in solution.
the NMR data (chemical shift values, coupling constants, and relaxation times) can be used to determine the "tautomerism" of NH-benzimadazoles in solution.
